headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: Over four weeks of losses; the month now leans clearly down

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Keep marketing and acquisition budgets at the planned level, but do not step them up: Bitcoin is down about 12% in a week and about 24% in a month, a Rally watch drop window has been open since 13 November, and the headline could turn BEARISH within days if the weakness lasts. Keep a reserve ready instead of cutting, because the long-run base is still rising; spend now on retention, trust and education, and on acquisition only once price closes back above the 200-week average ($68,390) and then the 200-day average ($72,645). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

watch: The headline still says NEUTRAL, but the medium-term reading has been in its weak zone for two days and would turn the headline BEARISH if it stays there a few more days. A close back above $68,390 (the 200-week average) would be the first sign the drop is easing; a close below $61,000 would deepen it.
analysis: Bottom line: Bitcoin is still sliding in a fearful market, so today is about holding steady and building trust, not pushing promotions. Short term, the mood is weak: at about $62,918 Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 29 days in a row, sits about 20% below it and about 25% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 10 out of 100. News is pulling this a little lower, as PANews reports S&P has rated the biggest stablecoin, USDT, 'weak' at holding its dollar value. A normal week lately swings about $3,782, so a close above $64,750 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $61,000 (the bottom of it) would turn it down further, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer messages fit far better than offers.

The next month leans down: the medium-term reading has now sat in its weak zone for two days, and if it stays there a few more days the headline would switch from NEUTRAL to BEARISH, while the long-term trend is still up. Price is about 24% lower than 30 days ago and about 20% lower than 90 days ago, and news adds a little weight, as the Fed's latest minutes (via PANews) say a bigger rate rise could be considered if inflation data disappoints. Bitcoin would have to win back $78,179 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. The Fed meeting on 8 December is the next scheduled event; keep bigger campaign pushes until after a clear turn.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but it is getting thin: the 200-day average is still rising (about 5% over 90 days), yet price is about 13% under it, about 8% under its 200-week average and about 50% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $72,645 (the 200-day average) again; $68,390 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has now slipped under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. News is adding a little here, as PANews reports Binance plans to expand into five Asian markets next year, Southeast Asia included, which also means more competition at home; more weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and be the time to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
